title: InnoEval: On Research Idea Evaluation as a Knowledge-Grounded, Multi-Perspective Reasoning Problem
one_liner: Evaluate research ideas by gathering outside evidence and letting reviewers with different backgrounds score the idea on separate criteria before seeking consensus.
lead: Generating research ideas has become easy for large language models. Judging which ideas are actually promising is harder, because good evaluation needs outside knowledge, multiple criteria, and disagreement between reviewers who notice different weaknesses. This paper builds an idea-evaluation pipeline that retrieves evidence from external sources and organizes several reviewer roles into a board that debates before producing a consensus judgment.

problem.h2: Why idea evaluation is harder than idea generation
paras: A raw idea score from one language model is easy to produce but hard to trust. The model may know only a narrow slice of the relevant literature, may collapse all evaluation criteria into one vague impression, and may carry its own judging bias from the prompt or training data.

Human reviewers do not evaluate ideas this way. They check what is already known, inspect the proposed contribution from different disciplinary angles, and weigh several criteria separately such as originality, feasibility, and likely impact. The paper argues that an idea-evaluation system should imitate that structure, because a single ungrounded score hides too much of the actual reasoning.

callout.html: Retrieve external evidence, assign several reviewer perspectives, score the idea on separate criteria, and then form a consensus judgment from those grounded partial views.

panels.title: 1. One judge is too narrow
panels.caption: A lone judge can miss literature and overcompress the decision.

panels.title: 2. Gather outside evidence
panels.caption: The system first collects information relevant to the idea.

panels.title: 3. Multiple reviewer roles
panels.viz_args: method reviewer | domain reviewer | impact reviewer
panels.caption: Different perspectives examine different failure modes.

panels.title: 4. Score separate criteria
panels.caption: The board avoids flattening everything into one first impression.

panels.title: 5. Consensus judgment
panels.caption: Consensus is formed after the separate views are compared.

steps.text: The system gathers outside sources that bear on the proposed idea, such as related methods, benchmarks, or earlier findings.
Several reviewer personas with different academic backgrounds are assigned so that each inspects the idea from a different angle.
Each reviewer evaluates dimensions such as originality, feasibility, and likely value instead of collapsing everything into one immediate score.
The board compares disagreements and evidence support so that unsupported enthusiasm or unsupported skepticism is challenged.
A final judgment is issued only after the evidence-grounded reviewer scores have been reconciled.

paras: The paper changes idea evaluation from a single-pass judgment into a structured decision process. The object is no longer one model's global score. It is a board-style evaluation made of external evidence, role-specific judgments, and explicit criteria.
object.object: The evaluation process: from one score to evidence-grounded board review

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: evidence-backed consensus quality
hidden.name: Evidence-backed consensus quality
paras: The hidden quantity is how trustworthy the final judgment is after combining knowledge coverage, criterion coverage, and reviewer agreement. High agreement alone is not enough, because reviewers can all agree for the wrong reason. High evidence coverage alone is not enough, because the evidence must still be interpreted correctly across criteria.

InnoEval aims to raise this quantity by grounding each reviewer in retrieved evidence and by forcing the board to compare several criteria explicitly. That reduces single-judge bias because a reviewer who is too optimistic on one dimension can be corrected by another reviewer with different evidence or a different evaluative focus.

heat.caption: The system is trying to improve the quality of consensus, not merely the loudness of agreement.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is how trustworthy the final board judgment is once evidence, criteria, and reviewer disagreement are all taken into account.
The framework treats idea evaluation as a knowledge-grounded multi-perspective reasoning problem, then seeks consensus only after evidence-backed criterion-level judgments have been formed.

paras: The mechanism works because each failure mode of naive judging is addressed by a corresponding structural component. Outside retrieval widens the knowledge base, so the evaluator is less likely to miss earlier related work or obvious feasibility obstacles. Multiple reviewer roles widen perspective, so one style of reasoning does not dominate every decision. Criterion-level scoring widens the decision surface, so a flashy idea cannot hide weak feasibility behind a strong originality impression.

Consensus comes last rather than first. That matters because early averaging often erases informative disagreement. By comparing evidence-backed partial judgments before merging them, the system can preserve useful reviewer differences long enough to identify what the idea is strong at, what it is weak at, and why the final decision should lean one way.

stages.s: Score separate criteria with evidence support

math.words: A final idea score can be written as a weighted sum of criterion scores, then adjusted by how well those scores are supported by retrieved evidence and reviewer agreement.
math.equation: final_score = sum over criteria of weight(c) * score(c) * evidence_support(c) * agreement(c)
symbols: board judgment on criterion c such as originality or feasibility
how strongly retrieved evidence supports that criterion judgment
how aligned the reviewers are on criterion c after deliberation
overall evaluation after combining all criteria

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose the idea has two criteria for a toy example: originality and feasibility.
Originality: weight 0.5, score 0.9, evidence support 0.8, agreement 0.9.
Feasibility: weight 0.5, score 0.6, evidence support 0.9, agreement 0.8.
The score is held back by feasibility because the board found weaker practical support there.

math.note: The exact aggregation can vary, but the key principle is to combine criterion value with evidence support instead of trusting an unsupported headline score.

charts.title: Single ungrounded judge
charts.note: One-pass judging misses too much because it lacks external evidence and explicit multi-criteria structure.

charts.title: InnoEval
charts.note: The structured board aligns better with expert judgment because it grounds the decision in evidence and separates the criteria before merging them.

items.b: Evidence retrieval misses key earlier work.
items.html: If the search stage omits key papers or benchmarks, the board can still reach a polished but weak conclusion because it is reasoning from incomplete evidence.
If all reviewer personas reason the same way, the board adds little beyond repetition. Consensus then rises for the wrong reason because diversity of viewpoint is missing.
If disagreement is averaged away before the supporting evidence is inspected, the system loses the very signal that could have revealed an important weakness.
Use broad evidence retrieval, define genuinely different reviewer perspectives, and delay consensus until criterion-level disagreements have been examined with the supporting sources.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Assemble a small benchmark of research proposals with expert judgments. Compare three evaluators: one single-judge language model, one multi-reviewer board without outside retrieval, and one full system with retrieval plus criterion-level board review. Score them on pointwise grading, pairwise preference between ideas, and groupwise ranking across a proposal set.
demo.metric_eq: expert_alignment = matching_decisions / total_decisions; ranking_quality = correctly_ordered_pairs / total_pairs
demo.closing: The demo should show that the full board aligns better with experts because it grounds each criterion in retrieved evidence before asking the reviewers to agree.
